No Way! Way!
NOH WAY — WAY
interjection, exchange (Gen X slang)
No way! ("impossible, I don’t believe it") is American slang from the mid-20th century. Its comic rebuttal Way! — turning the noun into a bare affirmative — became a catchphrase through the SNL "Wayne’s World" sketches (from 1989) and the film Wayne’s World (1992), where Wayne and Garth trade "No way!" "Way!" as a running bit. The exchange was quickly absorbed into schoolyard banter.

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

The Gen X exchange is a tiny argument about whether something is possible: "No way!" — "Way!" It sounds like nonsense, and that is the joke. But it is worth noticing which word the joke turned on. When the apostles first preached Christ, the movement had no name except this one: "any of this way" (Act 9:2). The Lord had said, "I am the way, the truth, and the life: no man cometh unto the Father, but by me" (Joh 14:6). To a world that says no way — no way to God, no way back from guilt, no way through death — the gospel answers, in effect, Way!: there is a Way, and He has a name. Scripture also warns against the false way that feels right: "There is a way which seemeth right unto a man, but the end thereof are the ways of death" (Pro 14:12). The Lord described two roads, the broad way that leads to destruction and the narrow way that leads to life, "and few there be that find it" (Mat 7:13-14). And Isaiah promised the guiding voice behind the believer: "This is the way, walk ye in it" (Isa 30:21). A father can play the game with a child and then turn it: when someone tells you there is no way to God, you know the answer — Way. His name is Jesus.

Webster 1828 Definition

Gen X comic exchange ("No way!" "Way!") from SNL’s "Wayne’s World" (1989–92); the gospel’s answer to every "no way" is the Way Himself (Joh 14:6).

expand to see more

NO WAY! WAY!, interj. (Gen X slang, 1989–early 1990s) A mock argument: disbelief ("No way!") met by insistence ("Way!").

No way (mid-20th-c. US): impossible, I don’t believe it. Way!: yes, really; the "Wayne’s World" rebuttal.

Often extended: "No way!" "Way!" "No way!" "Way!" — until someone laughs.

Webster 1828: WAY, n. [G., Latin] 1. Literally, a passing; hence, a passage; the place of passing; hence, a road of any kind; a highway; a private road; a lane; a street; any place for the passing of men; cattle or other animals; a word of very comprehensive signification. 2. Length of space; as a great way; a little way …

Decode for parents: the early church was called simply "the way" (Act 9:2); the gospel is God’s "Way!" to the world’s "no way."

Key Scripture

Joh 14:6 — "Jesus saith unto him, I am the way, the truth, and the life: no man cometh unto the Father, but by me."

Act 9:2 — "And desired of him letters to Damascus to the synagogues, that if he found any of this way, whether they were men or women, he might bring them bound unto Jerusalem."

Pro 14:12 — "There is a way which seemeth right unto a man, but the end thereof are the ways of death."

Mat 7:14 — "Because strait is the gate, and narrow is the way, which leadeth unto life, and few there be that find it."

Isa 30:21 — "And thine ears shall hear a word behind thee, saying, This is the way, walk ye in it, when ye turn to the right hand, and when ye turn to the left."

Modern Corruption

The exchange is harmless banter; the word it turns on is the oldest name of the church — "the way" — and the gospel is God’s "Way!" to a world that says there is no way to Him.

expand to see more

The world’s "no way." Modern unbelief says there is no way to know God, no way to be forgiven, no way past the grave — or, more fashionably, that there are many ways and none of them matters. Scripture answers both: there is a way that seems right and ends in death (Pro 14:12), and there is one Way that leads to the Father (Joh 14:6). The narrow way is narrow because it is a Person.

Walking the Way. The first Christians did not call themselves a religion; they were "of this way" (Act 9:2) — people on a road behind a Lord. The promise of Isaiah 30:21 is the believer’s comfort: a word behind you, saying, This is the way, walk ye in it.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Old English weg (road, path) → way; mid-20th-c. no way! → "Wayne’s World" rebuttal Way! (1989–92); Scripture: I am the way (Joh 14:6).

Old English weg — road, path, course of travel

Mid-20th-c. US: no way! — impossible, I don’t believe it

1989–92: Way! as comic rebuttal ("Wayne’s World")

The early church’s first name: "this way" (Act 9:2; Act 19:9)

Christ the Way (Joh 14:6); the narrow way to life (Mat 7:14)

Usage

""You got tickets to Metallica? No way!" "Way!""

"To the world’s "no way to God," the gospel says: Way — I am the way (Joh 14:6)."

"This is the way, walk ye in it (Isa 30:21)."
